passage: Kofi came home from school in Accra and dropped his bag by the door. “How was the test?” his older sister Dalia asked. “Fine.” “Did you eat lunch?” “Yes.” “Was Yaw there?” “No.” Each answer was short and flat, and he headed straight for his room. Dalia opened her mouth to ask more, then stopped. She thought he might be tired, or hurt about something, or just not ready. Instead she made two cups of hot chocolate, set one outside his door, and said, “I'm on the balcony if you want to talk.” Half an hour later, Kofi came out and sat down beside her.

qa.q: Where did Dalia sit after leaving the cup outside Kofi's door?
What did Dalia think Kofi's short answers might mean?
qa.a: She thought he might be tired, hurt about something or not ready to talk yet.

qa.q: Why was Dalia's plan better than asking more questions?
qa.a: It gave him time and a low-pressure moment, so he could come to her when he was ready.

qa.q: How might Kofi have felt about being asked so many questions right after school?
qa.a: He may have felt tired and wanted a quiet moment, so the questions could have felt like pressure.

grounding: Clipped replies after a hard day may mean tiredness, hurt or unreadiness, and offering time works better than demanding detail.

passage: After the afternoon bell, Akash walked into the school counselling room and dropped into a chair. Ms. Aparna asked, “How did the match go?” “Okay.” “Did you play well?” “Yeah.” “And your friends?” “Fine.” His replies were short, and he looked at the wall. She waited and then said, “You don't have to tell me now. I have some crayons and paper if you'd like to draw, and I'll be here till four.” Akash shrugged, but pulled the crayons over. Ten minutes later, without looking up, he said, “Ravi didn't pass me the ball all day.” Ms. Aparna nodded.

qa.q: How long did Ms. Aparna say she would be there?
What might Akash have been feeling when he gave clipped answers?
qa.a: He may have felt hurt about the match and not ready to talk, which explains why he only shared later about the ball.

qa.q: What did Ms. Aparna do that made it easier for Akash to share?
qa.a: She stopped pushing for detail and offered crayons and time, so he could talk when he was ready.

qa.q: How might Ravi's behaviour look to Akash, compared with how Ravi might see it?
qa.a: Akash felt left out of the game, while Ravi may not have realised his passing left Akash hurt.

grounding: A child with clipped answers after a hard match may be hurt or unready to talk, and the counsellor offers time.
